2  This application coming on for hearing this day, the co  following:
 ORDER

The present applicant is the complainant who has filed the application under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. has been filed for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted by the learned court below vide order dated 16.06.2022.
The complainant's case is that he had entered into an agreement for purchase of two properties from the respondents No.2 to 5 and paid an advance of Rs.10 lac for the same.
However, as the respondents were not executing the sale deed in his favour and registering the same, the applicant demanded that his earnest money of Rs.10 lac be returned.

Learned counsel for the respondents submits that the applicant has filed present application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted by the learned court below for alleged offences under Sections 420, 294, 506 of the IPC only on account of the period of limitation of three years for filing a civil suit having expired.

He further submits that the entire proceedings against the applicant is an abuse of process of the court and that there is no requirement for interference with the order passed by the learned court below granting anticipatory bail, as the applicant has failed to show any subsequent event which has taken place after the anticipatory bail was granted to show that the respondents No.2 to 5 have, by in any way, abused the conditions of anticipatory bail or have not cooperated to the police in the course of investigation.
He further submits that the grounds for cancellation of anticipatory bail once granted in far more onerous then the consideration that prevail at the time of granting a bail.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the order passed by the learned court below is unreasoned and is therefore, unsustainable in the eyes of law.

He further submits that learned trial court has only recorded the submissions of the respective parties and thereafter, granted anticipatory bail without arriving at a finding with regard to the necessity for granting anticipatory bail.

However, while going through the impugned order dated 16.06.2022 which runs into four pages, it appears that the learned court below has diligently recorded the submissions of both the sides and thereafter, it is also come to a finding in the internal page No.3 of the said order wherein the last paragraph, the learned trial court has observed that having gone through the case diary, it appears that the complainant has not given any document in support of his contentions that he had ever paid Rs.10 lac to the respondents herein.

One more ground was taken by the learned counsel for the respondents which that there is a telephonic conversation between the respondent No.2 and applicant herein wherein applicant has admitted to having received Rs.4,85,000/- from the Devendra Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196822760/
2 respondents.

sentences.text: He has further stated that the respondents are willing to pay the balance of Rs.5,20,000/- to the applicant as and when demanded by the applicant.
Per contra, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the said conversation has been denied by the complainant and not even a farthing has been given by the respondents to the applicant.

He further states that there is no forensic voice verification of the said recording on the basis of which any court would arrive at the finding that the respondents had already returned a part of the earnest money deposited with them by the applicant.

To this, learned counsel for the respondents submits that there is a report of the SDO which has gone through the said conversation and arrived at the finding that the respondents have paid back Rs.4,80,000/- of the earnest money of Rs.10 lac deposited with them.

Be that as it may, looking at the facts and circumstances of the case, and the fact that the anticipatory bail has been granted by the learned court below on brief but germane and cogent reasons and therefore, it calls for no interference by this court as there are no subsequent events warranting the cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the respondents.

At this juncture, respondent No.2 is present in person before this Court and has given an undertaking that as and when so demanded by the applicant, he shall pay the balance amount of Rs.5,20,000/- finally.
Under the circumstances, the application sans merit and is hereby dismissed.
